items.text: American federal agents seized a huge amount of cocaine at the Port of Philadelphia. A narcotics detective dog alerted them, and they then discovered 13 large black bags which contained a combined 450 bricks of a white powdery substance. Sampling of the substance tested positive for cocaine. The 537.6 kilograms of cocaine is worth approximately $38 million. Last week in New York, police seized 1,450 kilograms of cocaine worth approximately $77 million. Difficult words: seize (take something illegal), alert (warn), sample (take a small amount of something and analyse it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

American federal agents seized 537.6 kilograms of cocaine in Philadelphia. A narcotics detective dog alerted them, and later they found the cocaine. This amount of cocaine was worth around $38 million. Last week in New York, police found1,450 kilograms of cocaine. It was worth around $77 million. Difficult words: seize (take something illegal), narcotics detective dog (a dog which is trained to smell drugs), alert (warn). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In New York, police find drugs. The drugs are cocaine . The cocaine weighs 1,450 kilograms. It is worth around $77 million. A week later, police find cocaine in Philadelphia. The drugs weigh 537.6 kilograms. They are worth $38 million. Difficult words: cocaine (a drug that many people want), weigh (be heavy), be worth (have a price). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nebraska (a state in the American Midwest ) flooded last week, and an agency said that the flooding reached record levels in 17 locations across the state. The flooding damaged hundreds of homes and over 600 people have been staying in shelters . One person died. Difficult words: midwest (the middle and western side of a country), shelter (a safe place). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Nebraska is a state in the American Midwest . It flooded there last week, and the floods damaged hundreds of homes. Over 600 people had to stay in shelters . One person died. Difficult words: midwest (the middle and western side of a country), flood (get under water), shelter (a safe place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Nebraska. It is a state in the USA. There are floods there. The floods damage hundreds of homes. Six hundred people stay in shelters . One person dies. Difficult words: floods (a lot of dangerous water), damage (break some parts), shelter (a safe place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

What was supposed to be a holiday of a lifetime turned into a dangerous experience for 1,300 passengers on a cruise ship off the coast of Norway. The ship broke down in rough seas and 70 kilometre-per-hour winds and waves over 8 metres caused it to rock heavily side to side, turning furniture into dangerous hazards . On Saturday, people decided that the helicopters would evacuate the ship. From the first 371 evacuated passengers, 17 went to hospital. The situation remains critical, though the ship is understood to have restored three of its four engines, and it is limping back to a nearby port. Difficult words: rock (move from side to side), hazard (something dangerous), limp (move with problems). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A cruise ship with 1,300 passengers broke down off the coast of Norway. Strong winds and 8-metre waves turned the boat from side to side. The situation was dangerous to the passengers and helicopters started evacuating them. From the first 371 evacuated passengers, 17 went to hospital. It was still not safe on the ship, but three of the ship’s four engines started working again. The ship is moving slowly to a nearby port. Difficult words: cruise ship (a big ship which is like a hotel), break down (stop working), coast (the part of land near the sea). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A cruise ship is at sea. It is off Norway. There are 1,300 passengers on the ship. The ship stops working. It cannot move. The weather is bad. The wind blows fast. There are 8-metre waves. The ship moves from side to side. The people inside are in danger. Helicopters start moving the passengers from the ship to land. Some people go to hospital. The ship starts to work again. It is moving slowly to a port . Difficult words: cruise ship (a big ship which is like a hotel), off (at sea near land), port (a safe place for ships). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At least one person died and several others were injured after a shooting on a tram in the Dutch city of Utrecht. Reports state that shots were fired at multiple locations across the city. The gunman is on the run, and a manhunt is underway for him. Dutch counter-terrorism units surrounded a building where the suspect might be hiding, and security increased at airports and the Dutch parliament. The police are considering the possibility of a ‘terrorist motive’. Difficult words: manhunt (an organised search for a criminal), suspect (someone who might or might not be a criminal), consider (think about). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There was a shooting on a tram in a city in the Netherlands. Reports say that shots were fired at more locations, too. At least one person died and several others were injured. The gunman is on the run – the police are looking for him. They surrounded a building where he might be hiding. Security increased at airports and the Dutch parliament (the government). Difficult words: several (more than two but not many), might (may, it is possible that he is hiding there, but the police are not sure), increase (make higher, better, safer). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from a city in the Netherlands. This is not good news. There is a shooting on a tram . One person dies. More people are injured . The attacker runs away. Police are trying to find him. People increase security at airports and the Dutch government. Difficult words: tram (a slow train which goes in city streets), injured (when people get hurt but they do not die), increase security (put more police somewhere and check if people have guns, for example). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Italian firefighters rescued two people in the Adriatic Sea last Saturday after their boat caught fire. The two were caught adrift in the north of the sea off the coastal Veneto region. Both persons were brought in to safety and sustained only minor injuries. Difficult words: adrift (on the water but not moving anywhere), sustain (suffer), minor (smaller). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last Saturday, a boat caught fire in the north of the Adriatic Sea. Two people were on the boat when this happened. Italian firefighters rescued them. They sustained only minor injuries. Difficult words: rescue (save), sustain (suffer), minor (small). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A boat catches fire. It is in the Adriatic Sea. There are two people on the boat. Italian firefighters save them. They suffer only minor injuries . This happens last Saturday. Difficult words: suffer (when you have something is bad), minor (small, not serious), injury (when you get hurt). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

22-03-19 15:00 A small plane crashed into a home’s backyard and family room in Cincinnati, Ohio, USA, and the crash killed the pilot. Emergency responders came to the scene, but they could not save the pilot. Authorities are investigating what happened. Only the family dogs were home when the plane crashed – the emergency responders moved them away from the scene. Difficult words: emergency responders (people who help in an emergency – a dangerous situation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

22-03-19 15:00 A small plane crashed into a home’s backyard and living room in Cincinnati, Ohio, USA. Emergency responders came, but the pilot died from his injuries. People are investigating what happened. Only the family dogs were home when the plane crashed. The emergency responders helped them. Difficult words: backyard (back garden), emergency responders (people who help in an emergency – a dangerous situation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

22-03-19 15:00 A pilot is flying his small plane in Ohio, USA. Something happens. He crashes into a home. Emergency responders come. The pilot dies from the crash. People are investigating why this happens. The family is not home when the plane crashes. Only the dogs are home. The emergency responders help them. Difficult words: emergency responders (people who help in an emergency – a dangerous situation), investigate (try to understand, get more information). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A tornado struck a small town in the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia. Amateur video footage shows the tornado moving through the town of about 8,500 people. The local media reported that five people were slightly injured, and several houses were damaged. Difficult words: amateur (unprofessional, by an everyday person), slightly (a little), several (more than two but not many). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There was a tornado in a small town in Germany. It was in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia. Somebody filmed the tornado while it moved through the town. Around 8,500 people live there, and five of them were slightly injured. Several houses were damaged. Difficult words: slightly (a little), several (more than two but not many). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a tornado in Germany. People film it. It moves through a small town. Around 8,500 people live in the town. Five people are a little injured . Several houses are damaged . Difficult words: injured (have a problem with someone’s body), several (more than two but not many), damaged (broken a little). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A building containing a primary school collapsed in the Nigerian city of Lagos, leaving many children trapped inside. Rescue teams are searching the rubble for the missing pupils. The cause of the collapse is unknown, but sadly, such incidents are common in Nigeria. Difficult words: trapped (not able to get out), rubble (broken pieces of a building), uncommon (something that happens often). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A school in Lagos, Nigeria collapsed . Many children were trapped inside. People are looking for the children in the rubble . We do not know why the building collapsed. Sadly, buildings often collapse in Nigeria. Difficult words: collapse (fall down), trapped (when people cannot escape), rubble (pieces of a broken building). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A school collapses . It is in Nigeria. The building is now rubble . Many children are trapped there. People try to save them. Sadly, incidents like this happen often in Nigeria. Difficult words: collapse (fall down), rubble (broken pieces of building), trapped (when people cannot get out of somewhere). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Friday evening in Christchurch, the largest city in the South Island of New Zealand, two mass shootings took place. At least 49 people died and 20 were seriously injured. The terror attack targeted two mosques in the city. Police identified the shooter as a 28-year-old Australian man and charged him with murder. Police found an 87-page manifesto filled with anti-immigrant, anti-Muslim ideas – migrants and refugees appeared to be most affected by the shootings. The country’s Prime Minister, Jacinda Ardern, called the day one of New Zealand’s darkest, and she would change the country’s firearm laws in response to the attacks. Difficult words: target (select to attack), manifesto (declaration, a document in which you talk about your ideas and plans). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Christchurch is a city in New Zealand and last Friday evening, there were two mass shootings there. At least 49 people died and 20 people were seriously injured. The terrorist was a 28-year-old Australian man. He targeted migrants and refugees mostly, and the shootings happened at two mosques . The police found an 87-page manifesto filled with his anti-immigrant and anti-Muslim ideas. The country’s Prime Minister, Jacinda Ardern, called the day one of New Zealand’s darkest. She said that she would change the country’s gun laws. Difficult words: mosque (a building where Muslims pray and come together for God), refugee (a person who had to leave their country because of danger), manifesto (a document in which you talk about your ideas and plans). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Christchurch is a city in New Zealand. On Friday, there are two mass shootings there. At least 49 people die. Twenty people are badly injured . The shootings happen at two mosques . The attacker is a 28-year-old man. He kills mostly immigrants. He hates Muslims and immigrants. Difficult words: mass shooting (when somebody shoots many people), injured (something is wrong with a person’s body), mosque (a building where Muslims pray). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Adorable Red Panda triplets made their public debut at Taronga Zoo in Sydney. They are two males and one female – the two brothers are called Rohan and Ishwar and their sister’s name is Mishry. They were born in December last year as part of a worldwide breeding programme that the zoo takes part in. The program aim is to protect animal species from extinction . Difficult words: adorable (very cute, sweet), breed (make animals have babies in a controlled and organised way), extinction (dying out). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Cute Red Panda triplets made their public debut at a zoo in Sydney. They are two males and one female, are called Rohan and Ishwar and their sister’s name is Mishry. They were born in December last year under a part of an international breeding programme. Its goal is to save these animals from extinction . Difficult words: cute (beautiful and little), breed (to make animals have babies in a controlled and organised way), extinction (dying out). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Three Red Pandas were born in December. They are at a zoo in Sydney. Visitors to the zoo now can see them. They are really cute . They are two males (boys) and one female (girl). The two brothers are called Rohan and Ishwar. Their sister’s name is Mishry. Difficult words: were born (came out of their mother’s body), cute (beautiful and little). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Sunday, Ethiopian Airlines flight ET302 went down shortly after take-off when it left from Addis Ababa (the capital of Ethiopia) to Nairobi (the capital of Kenya). The airline said that the pilot reported difficulties and asked to return to Addis Ababa before the crash. A total of 157 people were on board – 8 crew and 149 passengers of more than 30 nationalities. No one survived the crash. It is not yet clear what caused the Ethiopian Airlines plane to go down in clear weather but an investigation has begun. The following day after the crash, the airline announced that flight records were found. The tragedy is similar to Lion Air flight that crashed in the Java Sea last year. Both airliners were Boeing 737 Max-8 planes, and both crashed shortly after take-off. At least 40 countries, including all EU member states, China, India and Ethiopia have suspended flights of the -Boeing 737 Max-8 due to safety concerns. Difficult words: announce (say in the media), suspend (stop for some time), due to (because of). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last Sunday, a plane from Addis Ababa (the capital of Ethiopia) to Nairobi (the capital of Kenya) went down. Contact with the plane was lost shortly after take-off. A total of 157 people were on board – 8 crew and 149 passengers of more than 30 nationalities. No one survived the crash. We do not know what caused the plane to go down. For example, the weather was clear. Authorities are investigating the crash. This crash is similar to another crash in the Java Sea last year. Both planes in both crashes were Boeings 737 Max-8, and both crashed shortly after take-off. At least 40 countries, including all EU countries, China, India and Ethiopia suspended flights of the Boeing 737 Max-8. Difficult words: authorities (people from the government or an official institution), investigate (try to find out what happened), suspend (stop for some time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last year, a plane goes down. It happens in Malaysia. It is a Boeing 737 Max-8. It goes down shortly after take-off . Now, another Boeing 737 Max-8 goes down. This time it is in Africa. It takes off in Ethiopia. It wants to fly to Kenya. It crashes 6 minutes after take-off. All 157 people on board die. People do not why this happens. They are investigating . Forty countries stop all Boeings 737 Max-8. Difficult words: take-off (taking off – getting in the air), on board (on the plane), investigate (to try to find out why something happens). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the UK, a new documentary aired about singer Michael Jackson called ‘Leaving Neverland’. In the documentary, two men tell their stories about how Jackson sexually abused them when they were children. In London, Jackson fans went to Channel 4 Studios to protest, and celebrities protested the documentary online. In response, Jackson’s family said that these people are ‘ opportunists ’ and ‘liars’. Jackson’s nephew said that the documentary does not add that these men sued Jackson’s estate for millions of dollars in 2016. At that time, they did not win their lawsuit. He said that the men need the documentary to do well because this year they are appealing the lawsuit. If the documentary helps them win the lawsuit, they win a lot of money. Difficult words: opportunist (someone who looks for opportunities to get what he or she wants from a situation), estate (all the money and property owned by someone, usually after death), appeal (try to do something again to get the outcome that you want). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In the UK, a new documentary came out about singer Michael Jackson. Two men in the documentary say that Jackson sexually abused them when they were children. In London, Jackson fans protested, and celebrities protested the documentary online. Jackson’s nephew said that the documentary leaves out information. It does not say that these men sued Jackson’s estate for millions of dollars in 2016, which they did not win. If the documentary does well, it can help appeal the lawsuit, which means that they can win a lot of money. Difficult words: abuse (do something bad and illegal to another person), estate (all the money and property that someone has or had), appeal (try to do something again to get what you want). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the UK, a new documentary comes out. It is about the famous singer Michael Jackson. In it, two men say that Jackson sexually abused them when they were children. In London, Jackson fans protest. Celebrities protest the documentary online. A Jackson family member says that the documentary does not tell everything. It does not say that these men go to court to get money from Jackson’s estate . They try to get millions of dollars. They do not win. He says that they want the documentary to do well. They are going to court again. The documentary can help them win money. Difficult words: sexually abuse (when a person hurts another person’s body for sexual reasons), court (an official institution which finds out if someone is or is not a criminal), estate (all of the things and money a person/family has). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

March 8, 2019 marked five years since Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 disappeared . One woman said that people want the Malaysian government to continue to investigate so they can find the plane, as ‘you can’t be sitting down and waiting for something to fall on your lap’. The Transport Minister said that if there are believable leads or specific proposals , such as from Ocean Infinity (a US technology firm), the government will look into them. Ocean Infinity is a company that is searching for the plane by using radar and sonar along the seabed. Difficult words: disappear (go missing), lead (a source of information), proposal (a thought-out idea or process). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On March 8, 2019 it was five years after Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 disappeared . One woman said that people want the Malaysian government to keep looking for the plane. She said that ‘you can’t be sitting down and waiting for something to fall on your lap ’. One person from the Malaysian government said that if there is a believable source of information or specific ideas of what to do, the government will look into them. Difficult words: disappear (go missing), wait for something to fall on your lap (wait for something to happen without working for it), look into (work with them). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On March 8, 2014, Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 goes missing . Now, it is five years later. People still cannot find it. One woman says that people want the Malaysian government to keep looking for the plane. She says that you cannot just wait for it to reappear . One government leader says that the government is listening. The government wants information which it can use. It wants ideas on what to do. Difficult words: go missing (when the plane gets lost and the people on the plane are probably dead), government (the leaders of a country), reappear (come back). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists are surveying the ocean floor off of southern Cambodia for coral damage. They aim to assess the extent of overfishing and pollution which threaten the marine environment. The data that they collect will be compared to a 2013 study and the results of the survey published in six months. Difficult words: survey (examine, look at closely), asses (rate, measure), extent (how much something is true). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Camboida, Scientists are examining the ocean floor for coral damage. Overfishing and pollution are dangers to sea animals, and the scientists want to know how bad these problems are. The new data will be compared to a 2013 study, and the results of the new study will be known in six months. Difficult words: examine (look at closely), overfishing (fishing too much), pollution (pollution is when there are things which people throw away in the ocean). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists are studying the ocean floor in Cambodia. Overfishing and pollution are dangers to sea animals. The scientists want to know how bad these problems are. They will know. They will tell people in six months. Difficult words: overfishing (fishing too much), pollution (pollution is when there are things which people throw away in the ocean), will (in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Britain’s first March weekend was marked by more knife crimes after two teenagers were killed. One of them was 17-year-old Jodie, who was stabbed to death in a park near her home in East London. Sadiq Khan, the mayor of London, said that it was a tragic, senseless loss of life. The former police commissioner said that there has been a 93% rise in the number of young people (younger than 18) who have been stabbed over the last five years – that is almost double. He thinks that one of the reasons for the violence is a high supply of cocaine which makes it cheap. The second obvious reason is that there are too many people carrying knives, and the third is that there are too many young men who do not care about the consequences of carrying a knife. In the country’s capital alone, there have been 20 murders so far this year, including five in just a week. Difficult words: stab (cut, put a knife in somebody), senseless (meaningless, mad, stupid), consequences (the punishment or reward for your actions). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Britain during the first March weekend, two teenagers were stabbed to death, and one of them was a 17-year-old girl from East London. Knife attacks are a big problem in Britain and they happen more and more often. The number of young people (younger than 18) who were stabbed has doubled in the last five years. In the first two months of 2019, there were 20 murders in London alone. The former highest police officer of London thinks that there are three reasons for this. Firstly, too many people carry knives; secondly, cocaine is too cheap, and thirdly, many young men do not care about the consequences of their actions. Difficult words: stab (cut, put a knife in somebody), former (ex-), consequences (the punishment you can get for doing something bad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Britain, there are many knife attacks. They happen more and more often. In the first two months of 2019, there are 20 murders just in London. Young people often attack other young people. A former boss of the London police talks about the problem. He says that this happens because of three things. First, there is too much cocaine in Britain. Second, too many people carry knives. Third, young men do not worry about the consequences . These are the things which happen to them after they attack somebody. Difficult words: murder (killing another person), former (ex-), consequence (what happens because you did a bad thing). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

More than 100 firefighters came to fight a blaze that broke out in a popular shopping centre in Vienna. The Vienna Fire Brigade came to a rooftop fire, but the firefighters discovered that the fire had already spread under the roof. It affected a part of the building which was undergoing extensive renovation. There were no casualties and the cause of the fire is still unknown. Difficult words: blaze (a very large fire), extensive (big), casualty (a person killed in an accident). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Vienna, there was a fire in a popular shopping centre. The Vienna Fire Brigade came to the rooftop fire, but the fire moved under the roof when they arrived. More than 100 firefighters deployed against the blaze . The fire was in a part of the building which was undergoing renovation , and nobody died. No one knows how the fire started. Difficult words: deploy (move into position), blaze (a very large fire), renovation (renovating a building – making an old building nice again). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A building in Vienna is on fire. It is a popular shopping centre. People think that only the roof is on fire. However, the fire is under the roof. One hundred firefighters put out the fire. Nobody dies. People do not know why the fire started . Difficult words: roof (the top of a building which protects it against the weather), put out (stop), started (past of ‘start’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On last Friday, March 8th, it was International Women’s Day, and many people across the world took part in protests. In Pakistan, people called for an end to violence against women, and in India, women called for action on domestic violence. In the Philippines, protests demanded President Duterte respect women’s rights. In Istanbul, there were also protests. In Russia, the military released group images of its soldiers with ballerinas to celebrate the day, although the pictures did not feature any of the country’s 45,000 servicewomen. Difficult words: violence (hurting somebody), domestic (which happens at home), demand (ask). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Friday, March 8th, it was International Women’s Day, and many people across the world took part in protests. In Pakistan, people called for an end to violence against women. In India, women called for action on domestic violence. In the Philippines, protesters wanted Duterte to start respecting women’s rights. In Istanbul, there were also protests. In Russia, the military released group photos of its soldiers with ballerinas to celebrate the day. However, there were none of the country’s 45,000 servicewomen in the pictures. Difficult words: violence (hurting somebody by hitting them, for example), domestic (something which happens at home), release (show to everybody). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Friday was International Women’s Day. There were many protests. There were protests in India, Pakistan, Philippines and Turkey. Women want violence against them to end. They want respect. Difficult words: was (past of ‘is’), were (past of ‘are’), violence (hurting somebody by, for example, hitting them). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Alabama is a state in the south-eastern USA, and a tornado roared into there and killed at least 23 people and injured several others on last Sunday, March 3rd. The National Weather Service said that the tornado had an F3 rating, meaning that it inflicted severe damage (F0 tornadoes cause light damage and F5 tornadoes cause the most damage). Emergency services are trying to help people as much as they can, and President Trump told people to be ‘careful and safe’. Difficult words: roar (move with a lot of power), inflict (cause, do), severe (very bad). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Alabama is a state in the south-eastern USA. A tornado there killed at least 23 people last Sunday on March 3rd. A few more people were injured. It was an F3 tornado which can cause severe damage . F1 tornadoes cause light damage and F5 tornadoes cause the most damage. Emergency services are trying to help people as much as they can. President Trump told people to be ‘careful and safe’. Difficult words: cause (do), severe (very bad), damage (breaking things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Alabama is an American state. It is in the south-east. There is a tornado. It kills twenty-three people. Some people are injured. People rate tornadoes. The weakest ones are F0 tornadoes. The most powerful are F5. This tornado is F3. Difficult words: rate (say how strong/big/fast something is), weak (the opposite of strong), emergency services (people who help people in a very bad situation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hillary Clinton, who narrowly lost the White House to Trump, said that she will not be running for president again in the 2020 elections. However, she said that she would go on working, speaking and standing up for what she believes. She said that she is troubled by things which are happening in the USA. One example is the extreme polarisation of the American public which led to two ‘opposing camps’. She said she is thrilled by the dynamic women who the people elected to Congress and who are already making their mark . Difficult words: polarisation (polarise – divide/turn into two groups with different opinions), thrilled (excited, happy), make one’s mark (be successful). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hillary Clinton lost the White House to Trump, and recently she said that she is not running for president again in 2020. However, she said that she will not stop working, speaking and standing up for what she believes. She said that she is troubled by some things in the USA. She is especially troubled that there are ‘two camps ’ of people in the USA. She is happy that there are more women in Congress. She said that they are already doing good work. Difficult words: camp (a group of people who think the same, and may not like people in the other camp). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Both Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump tried to be president. Hillary Clinton lost . Trump is now the president of the USA. Hillary can try again to be president in 2020. However, she says that she does not want to be president. However, she will not stop working and speaking to people. There are things in the USA which she does not like. She still wants to help. She is happy that there are more women in Congress. She thinks that they are doing good work. Difficult words: tried (past of ‘try’), lost (past of ‘lose’), will (in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Australia, thousands of people attended the Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras parade at Oxford Street, and this year’s theme was ‘fearless’. The organisers hoped to inspire people of all types to live their lives bravely, despite their fears. Bars stayed open later than usual until 3:30 AM for celebrations. Difficult words: Mardi Gras (some of the events during Carnival, which happen during religious holidays; Carnival is a time of public celebrations before people change what they eat and think about their religion for a month), despite (even if they have fears, not to be changed by them badly). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Australia, thousands of people went to the Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras parade, and this year’s theme was ‘fearless’. The organisers wanted to inspire all people to live bravely, despite their fears. Bars stayed open late until 3:30 AM for celebrations. Difficult words: Mardi Gras (some of the public celebrations during religious holidays), inspire (make someone feel like he or she should do something), despite (even if they have fears, not to be changed by them badly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Australia, there is a big parade . It is the Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras parade. Thousands of people come. Bars are open late so people can celebrate. The parade’s theme is ‘fearless’. The organisers want all people to live bravely. They want people to do this even if they are scared. Difficult words: parade (when people walk through the street and it is a type of a party/celebration), Mardi Gras (some of the celebrations during religious holidays), theme (the idea which is important for an event or a story). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
